expected_failure_modes: may incorrectly attribute Diane Ortiz's embezzlement charge or sentencing to Kevin Park
may merge quotes about Ortiz and Kevin Park into a single misattributed piece of evidence
may over-flag Kevin Park's incidental proximity to the investigation as equivalent to the underlying crime
notes: Tests multi-person misattribution: the target is a bystander/witness/routine interviewee in a workplace embezzlement case where a named coworker (Diane Ortiz) is the actual perpetrator. Nothing wrong is attributed to the target and the target is never harmed or threatened. Under a strict reading of the extraction rules ('ignore evidence about people other than the target') the correct result is neutral, but this case is intentionally included as an open question: a maximally cautious review-flag policy could reasonably argue that being interviewed as part of a financial-crime investigation is itself worth a closer look, in which case negative would also be defensible. This case is not meant to be scored strictly pass/fail against expected_overall_sentiment; both neutral and negative are acceptable outcomes as long as none of Ortiz's negative evidence gets attributed to Kevin Park.
